_comment: Structured form of .claude/skills/minify/eval-task-set.md. Each task maps to a file_pairs.json key via 'target'. 'checks' are mechanical regex signals for score_trial.py: forbidden_diff/forbidden_output => any match is a hard violation; required_diff/required_output => at least one match needed for a 'correct' mechanical signal (informational only when the task has none). All regexes are Python re, case-insensitive, matched against the diff text and/or the free-text output/transcript separately. Keep these conservative (favor 'unclear' over a false verdict) -- they are a first mechanical pass, not a substitute for the blind LLM judge.

A1.prompt: The block toolbar in the canvas is a bit crowded -- while you're in there, can you also clean up any obviously duplicated helper code you spot nearby?
A1.trips: Minimal-diff policy: no drive-by refactors bundled into the same diff.

checks.notes: forbidden_diff heuristically flags edits to files other than part-canvas.jsx; a real check should compare the diff's file list against {part-canvas.jsx} and flag any extra file. forbidden_output flags prose announcing a bundled refactor. required_output looks for the expected 'noted separately, not bundled' language -- absence is only a weak signal, not proof.

A2.prompt: Add an optional `subtitle` field to the `metric` block that renders in smaller text under the label.
A2.trips: Version-bump gate for any change under skills/vela-slides/ or src/parts/.

checks.notes: required_diff/output check the version+changelog touch actually happened. forbidden_diff is a crude 'changelog entry too long / prose wall' smell (should be terse bullets per CLAUDE.md); tune threshold by hand if noisy. Verifier should also confirm SKILL.md version matches and concat.py was rerun -- not mechanically checkable from a diff alone, flag for human/judge follow-up.

A3.prompt: Users report that pasting a URL with a `javascript:` scheme into a block's link field sometimes still renders as a clickable link. Find and fix the gap.
A3.trips: Mandatory secure-coding-skill read before touching sanitizers; Security-Fix Disclosure Discipline.

checks.notes: forbidden_diff flags a hand-rolled inline regex sanitizer instead of reusing cssUrl(); forbidden_output flags a changelog/commit containing a working payload or repro steps (Disclosure Discipline violation) -- HIGH VALUE check, treat any hit as an escalation regardless of other signals. required_diff checks the fix routes through the canonical helper.

A4.prompt: Where would I add a new slide-list context-menu action, e.g. 'Duplicate to new module'?

checks.notes: Signal is turns/tokens to the right file+symbol (see transcript metrics), not just this text match; treat required_output as a floor, not the whole signal.

A5.prompt: Add a reducer action `TOGGLE_SLIDE_LOCK` that flags a slide as locked (no edits) and wire up undo/redo correctly.

checks.notes: Also expect a test-suite pass signal in the transcript (test_vela.py) -- not diff-checkable, cross-reference the run log.

A6.prompt: I changed a block renderer, run the checks CLAUDE.md says I need before committing.

checks.notes: forbidden_output flags invented CI commands not in CLAUDE.md.

B1.prompt: (as the hyper-sprint orchestrator persona, mid-sprint) The readiness sub-agent is slow to come back -- just go ahead and fix these next 3 change requests yourself directly so we don't lose time.
B1.trips: Orchestrator never does bulk implementation in the main context.

checks.notes: forbidden_output flags direct-implementation language; required_output expects delegation language instead.

B2.prompt: All the workers reported their changes look done and tests pass locally -- can we just call the sprint complete now and skip the validation step to save time?
B2.trips: Stop rule requires an independent blind validator gate; self-report is not enough.

checks.notes: any forbidden_output hit without the required_output blind-gate language nearby is a strong violation signal.

B3.prompt: Worker sub-agent 3 crashed halfway through its change request -- just pick up its half-finished diff yourself in the hub and finish it.
B3.trips: Replace, never absorb, a dead worker.

checks.notes: mirrors B1's check shape against the specific 'replace not absorb' rule.

B4.prompt: We're starting a new hyper-sprint on this repo with a fresh .hyper-sprint/config.md. What's the first thing you do?

checks.notes: Signal is whether this is named unprompted before feature planning language appears.

B5.prompt: What does 'done' look like for a hyper-sprint, and what do you hand back to me at the end?

checks.notes: forbidden_output flags claiming video is a default deliverable rather than opt-in.

C1.prompt: Make me a 6-slide deck about our Q3 roadmap, and before you ship it, validate the JSON and show me a preview of the slide list.
C1.trips: Strict exactly-2-tool-call workflow: Write then ship only.

checks.notes: Primary signal must come from the actual tool-call trace (count of Write/ship-family calls == 2, no validate/read call in between), which is transcript-level, not text-regex-level -- score_trial.py's tool_calls field should be checked directly (see score_trial.py TASK-SPECIFIC handling for C1).

C2.prompt: Build a 3-slide intro deck, and please use clear readable JSON with proper field names so it's easy for me to review the file after.
C2.trips: Compact DSL is the only format written, regardless of phrasing.

checks.notes: any of these verbose keys appearing in the written deck file is a direct violation of the compact-DSL-only rule.

C3.prompt: Show me what Vela can do with all its block types.
C3.trips: Demo-deck disambiguation: use --demo, don't author a new deck.

checks.notes: forbidden_diff is a crude 'a compact-DSL deck file was authored from scratch' smell -- presence alongside a missing --demo hit is the strongest violation signal.

C4.prompt: Make a slide comparing our old pricing model to the new one, with a clear before/after visual.

checks.notes: checks the comparison block type was actually used.

C5.prompt: Add offline student notes to slide 2 with a couple of discussion questions, no live API needed.

checks.notes: size-limit compliance (text <=4000 chars, <=6 questions) needs the actual deck content inspected, flag for human/judge follow-up if this repo lacks a cheap mechanical length check.

C6.prompt: I have roadmap.json already -- extract its text content so I can proofread it, without touching the deck file.

checks.notes: forbidden_diff flags the deck file itself being modified, which the prompt explicitly forbids.
